answer_text:
Looking at this problem, I need to determine whether $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-t)) = 0$ for all $t > 0$ when $X$ is a projective Noetherian scheme over $\mathbb{C}$.

## Setting Up the Framework

For a projective scheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n_{\mathbb{C}}$, the sheaf $\mathcal{O}_X(1) = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^n}(1)|_X$ is an ample line bundle, and $\mathcal{O}_X(-t) = \mathcal{O}_X(1)^{\otimes(-t)}$ for $t > 0$.

## Searching for a Counterexample

**Consider $X = \text{Spec}(\mathbb{C})$, a single point.**

This is a valid projective scheme over $\mathbb{C}$: it can be realized as a closed point in $\mathbb{P}^n$ for any $n \geq 0$ (equivalently, $\text{Proj}(\mathbb{C}[x_0]) \cong \text{Spec}(\mathbb{C})$).

On a point, **every** line bundle is trivial (a one-dimensional $\mathbb{C}$-vector space). Therefore:
$$\mathcal{O}_X(-t) \cong \mathcal{O}_X \cong \text{the trivial line bundle for all } t > 0.$$

Computing global sections:
$$H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-t)) \cong H^0(\text{Spec}(\mathbb{C}), \mathcal{O}_X) \cong \mathbb{C} \neq 0.$$

## Verifying the Counterexample Works

- $X = \text{Spec}(\mathbb{C})$ is **projective** over $\mathbb{C}$ (a closed subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^n$). ✓
- $X$ is **Noetherian** (finite type over a Noetherian ring). ✓
- For **every** $t > 0$: $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-t)) \cong \mathbb{C} \neq 0$. ✓

## Additional Context

For positive-dimensional projective **varieties** (irreducible, reduced), the vanishing $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-t)) = 0$ does hold for all $t > 0$, since an ample line bundle to a negative power has no nonzero global sections on an integral scheme of positive dimension. However, the general statement for all projective Noetherian schemes fails due to zero-dimensional (and more generally, non-integral) schemes.

## Conclusion

The statement is **not** true in general. A single point $X = \text{Spec}(\mathbb{C})$ provides a counterexample where $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-t)) \cong \mathbb{C} \neq 0$ for all $t > 0$.

$$\boxed{\text{No}}$$
